title: Activities to prepare an essay about the future of tourism in Iraq
summary: The page presents a travel magazine advert inviting readers to write an essay on the future of tourism, followed by exercises to group tourism ideas under topics like accommodation and public transport, and to classify connectors by their function.

title: Writing task: an essay on the future of tourism in Iraq
summary: Students are asked to write a 100–120 word essay titled 'The future of tourism in Iraq', covering accommodation, public transport, types of holidays, tours, and their own topic, using connectors to link ideas.

title: Reading comprehension exercises about the importance of holidays
summary: The page includes multiple-choice questions and sentence-completion tasks based on a text about why holidays are important, covering matching headings with paragraphs and checking understanding of key ideas.
section: Lesson 9: Why are holidays so important?

title: Vocabulary, word completion, and discussion activities about holidays
summary: Exercises include finding synonyms in the text, completing words with missing vowels (such as workaholic and sightseeing), and partner discussion questions about work, breaks, and holiday preferences.

title: Revision exercises on compound nouns and relative pronouns
summary: Students complete dialogues by forming compound nouns related to travel, and combine sentence pairs into single sentences using appropriate relative pronouns with commas where necessary.

title: Revision exercises on present perfect and relative pronouns
summary: Tasks include completing sentences with the present perfect simple choosing between 'since' and 'for', filling in relative pronouns with commas, and selecting the correct option in multiple-choice grammar questions.

title: Vocabulary test with compound nouns, collocations, and adjective formation
summary: The test requires writing compound nouns from definitions, choosing the correct collocations in sentences, and forming adjectives from given nouns and verbs with correct endings.

title: Grammar test distinguishing present perfect from past simple
summary: Students identify correct and incorrect sentences using present perfect or past simple, then rewrite the six incorrect ones, covering topics like daily routines and recent actions.
